feedback.problem: If the line $y=-x+5$ and the curve $y=\frac{2}{x-5}+2$ intersect at the point $(p,q),$ then $p+q=$
feedback.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=-x+5 &  \\ y=\frac{2}{x-5}+2\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get a quadratic equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+5 & =\frac{2}{x-5}+2 \\ -x+3 & =\frac{2}{x-5} \\ (-x+3)(x-5) & =2 \\ -{x}^{2}+8x-15 & =2 \\ {x}^{2}-8x+17 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the quadratic formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{-(-8)\pm \sqrt{(-8)^{2}-4(1)(17)}}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{8\pm \sqrt{64-68}}{2} \\  & =\frac{8\pm \sqrt{-4}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root of a negative number is not a real number, so there are no real solutions. Consequently, the line $y=-x+5$ does not intersect the hyperbola $y=\frac{2}{x-5}+2.$
